subject: botany_2
question_text: Name the processes which take place in the grana and stroma regions of chloroplasts.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.40, printed question 63. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05: the second s1_grana common mistake was replaced, because it condemned the word thylakoid although the light reaction does take place on the thylakoid membranes of the grana, and the printed question already supplies both region names.

insider_note: Two words, two places. Naming the reaction without naming the region, or the other way round, answers half the question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Grana
steps.margin_note: Reaction name plus region. Three lines.
lines: The LIGHT REACTION takes place in the GRANA of
It is also called the photochemical phase.
steps.why: The grana hold the chlorophyll-bearing thylakoid membranes, so the reaction that needs light has to happen there.
common_mistakes: Saying the dark reaction happens in the grana. The LIGHT reaction does.
Naming only one of the two. The question asks for a process in each region — the light reaction in the grana AND the dark reaction in the stroma.
steps.memory_tip: Grana are green stacks: green catches light.

steps.label: Stroma
steps.margin_note: Mirror the grana line. The contrast is the whole answer.

lines.text: Light in the grana, carbon in the stroma

lines: The DARK REACTION (carbon fixation) takes place
in the STROMA of the chloroplast.
It is also called the biosynthetic phase.
steps.why: The Calvin cycle enzymes are dissolved in the stroma, so the carbon reactions happen in the fluid rather than on the membranes.
common_mistakes: Calling the dark reaction 'the reaction in darkness'. It does not need darkness, only that it does not use light directly.
Swapping the two regions. Grana for light, stroma for dark.
steps.memory_tip: Stroma is the fluid, and the sugar is built in it.
